title: Steep
provenance: Reported by Sean-Shmulevich (highball-db#465, 2026-10-12), Apple M2 Pro with 16 GB, macOS 26.3.1, a Highball CLI built from source at gin 0e0eb5d, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r21, D3DMetal with d3d10, d3d10_1 and d3d10core disabled, msync, AVX advertised, 1280x720 capped at 30 fps, rated 5 of 5 after a short session. steep.exe was started directly, so the Steam and Ubisoft sign-in path was not tested. Not verified by the maintainer.
notes: Reported working on an M2 Pro with D3DMetal once DirectX 10 is turned off for it. In D3DMetal mode a 64-bit game that loads DirectX 10 gets DXMT's d3d10core, which asks D3DMetal's Direct3D 11 for a function it does not have, and Steep stopped right at start with 'unimplemented function D3D11.DLL.D3D11CoreCreateDevice'. Setting the DLL overrides to d3d10,d3d10_1,d3d10core=d fixed it. DXMT refused the game's 8-sample texture on that Mac, and DXVK started but drew stretched menus and ran slowly. Long sessions and online play are untested.

knownIssues.symptom: In D3DMetal mode the game stops at start with 'Call to unimplemented function D3D11.DLL.D3D11CoreCreateDevice, aborting'
knownIssues.cause: the game loads DirectX 10, and in D3DMetal mode the 64-bit d3d10core comes from DXMT, which needs a Direct3D 11 function D3DMetal does not export
knownIssues.fix: set the environment's DLL overrides (Full page, Advanced) to d3d10,d3d10_1,d3d10core=d and keep D3DMetal

knownIssues.symptom: DXMT refuses an 8-sample texture and the game does not start
knownIssues.cause: the Mac's GPU offers 1, 2 or 4 samples, not 8
knownIssues.fix: use D3DMetal with DirectX 10 turned off as above
